title: ‘Love of Your Life’ Review: Margaret Qualley Goes on a Pretty but Surface-Level Healing Journey
content:
Rachel Morrison's second film as director follows a young nurse, bereaved during the global pandemic, as she grieves, escapes and returns to herself.

ByGuy Lodge

Film Critic

It would probably be glib to refer to “Love of Your Life” as “Grieve Pray Love.”Rachel Morrison‘s film about COVID-era loss, recovery and renewal is serious in intent and earnest in execution, grounded by a performance of intelligence and emotional transparency byMargaret Qualley, and doesn’t deserve that kind of easy dismissal. But the temptation is there. It’s hard not to think a little bit of Elizabeth Gilbert’s globe-trotting memoir “Eat Pray Love,” the epitome of breezy Noughties self-help entertainment, not to mention Ryan Murphy’s vapid, glowingly shot film adaptation, when watching this story of a bereaved young woman’s long-term recuperation via perfectly picturesque travels in Lisbon, London, Tokyo and beyond. There’s certainly much to be said for literal escape as a healing strategy, but Morrison’s permanently luminous film too often feels like a magazine spread about that process.

For viewers after a grownup romantic drama with equal, counterbalancing side servings of tearjerking trauma and glossy wish-fulfillment, “Love of Your Life” will handsomely suffice, and ought to rack up considerable streaming numbers when it hits Prime Video on Oct. 14, one month after its Toronto festival premiere. Amazon MGM Studios will also give it a brief theatrical release ahead of that date, but despite the soothing eye-bath of its protagonist’s well-curated world tour, the film never feels altogether cinematic: It’s as attractively mounted as you’d expect from cinematographer-turned-director Morrison (Oscar-nominated for her lensing of “Mudbound”) and her own chosen DP Todd Benhazl (“Hustlers”), but their radiant, exactingly lit images don’t collectively accrue much meaning or power; the film plods through its eight-year timeline with efficient linearity but no particular rhythm.

There’s life inside it, though, and that’s largely thanks to Qualley, a reliably curious and open-hearted actor who can imbue even quite a vaguely drawn character — like the one that screenwriter Julia Cox (“Nyad”) hands her here — with some sense of a soul. When we meet 26-year-old Maya (Qualley), completing a Craigslist purchase of a bedside table from instantly smitten academic Charlie (Gabriel Basso, still in recovery from playing J.D. Vance in “Hillbilly Energy”), she’s barely anybody at all: a nurse, in Boston, with no family she’s willing to mention, and no life outside her grueling hospital shifts. Qualley locates defensive purpose in Maya’s stiff reserve, and an errant gleam of joy when Charlie’s dorky come-ons actually do the job.

Before long, they’ve moved in together, setting up a perfectly boho-chic love nest in their Victorian apartment. Not too much later, they spring a surprise wedding on their loved ones, to the unspoken but visible consternation of Charlie’s world-weary mom Ruth (ensemble MVPCatherine Keener), and broach the possibility of starting a family — something Maya had always sworn off doing. And all too soon after that, a certain global pandemic strikes, and the worst thing that can happen to our heroine, well, happens. Plunged into the lightless tunnel vision of debilitating grief, she spurns the company of Ruth and longtime best friend Jason (Patrick Schwarzenegger, in a thankless part) and abruptly skips town before anyone can so much as trouble her with funeral arrangements. It’s a selfish trauma response that Qualley, seemingly body-slammed and hollowed-out with pain, makes almost rational.

Everything that happens from this point on in “Love of Your Life,” however, is considerably harder to swallow. We lurch forward a couple of years to find Maya — now 31 years old, aggressively kohl-eyed and constantly smoking — skulking the gorgeous streets of Lisbon, finding little emotional relief or release in its exquisite painted tiles andpasteis de nata, though plentiful cheapvinho verdeis evidently some comfort. But when she meets cute with Felix (Aaron Pierre), an absurdly good-looking touring Brit, she embraces the possibility of romance again, following him first to a Condé Nast-ready holiday home in rural Portugal, and then back to his well-appointed life in West London, complete with adorable young daughter. (He’s a doting single dad on great terms with the girl’s mom, lest you fear this impossible dreamboat may have even a whisper of a character flaw.)

None of this even remotely resembles real life, which makes Maya’s emotional recovery increasingly hard to map: We learn in passing that she’s somehow funding these extended, luxurious travels with a career segue into telehealth, and when her online therapist observes that “we’re really getting somewhere,” we just have to take her word for it. Cox’s script, meanwhile, trades increasingly in one-size-fits-all therapy speak, and despite Qualley’s natural sincerity as a performer, Maya seems steadily less specific a personality as the years pass.

Late in proceedings, “Love of Your Life” gets a welcome jolt of feeling and truth from a scene that reunites Maya with Ruth, beautifully played by Keener with all the shattered, visible exhaustion of a woman who hasn’t got to nurture her grief in the Algarve sun. As she unpacks her damage, frankly but no longer angrily, against the unphotogenic greige backdrop of her house’s timber siding, “Love of Your Life” finally reconnects with reality, and not a moment too soon.
title_zh: 《你生命中的愛(Love of Your Life)》影評：瑪格·夸莉(Margaret Qualley)展開了一段美麗但表面化的療癒之旅
content_zh:
瑞秋·莫里森(Rachel Morrison)的第二部導演作品講述了一位年輕護士在全球疫情中失去摯愛後，如何悲傷、逃避並重新找到自我的故事。

作者：蓋·洛奇(Guy Lodge)

影評人

將《你生命中的愛》(Love of Your Life) 稱為“悲傷祈禱愛”(Grieve Pray Love) 可能有些輕率。瑞秋·莫里森(Rachel Morrison)的這部關於COVID時代失落、康復和重生的電影在意圖上是嚴肅的，執行上也很真誠，並且由瑪格·羅利(Margaret Qualley)的智慧和情感透明的表演所支撐，並不值得這種輕易的貶低。但這種誘惑確實存在。在觀看這位失去摯愛的年輕女性通過在里斯本、倫敦、東京等地的完美旅行來進行長期康復的故事時，很難不聯想到伊莉莎白·吉爾伯特(Elizabeth Gilbert)的環球旅行回憶錄《飲食祈禱愛》(Eat Pray Love)，這是輕鬆的零零年代自助娛樂的典範，更不用提瑞安·墨菲(Ryan Murphy)那部空洞、光鮮的電影改編作品。對於字面上的逃避作為療癒策略，確實有很多話要說，但莫里森的這部永遠光輝的電影常常讓人感覺像是一篇關於這個過程的雜誌特寫。

對於尋找一部成熟浪漫劇情片的觀眾來說，《你生命中的愛》將會非常滿足，並且在10月14日登陸Prime Video時，應該會獲得相當可觀的串流觀看數，這距離其在多倫多影展的首映僅一個月。亞馬遜MGM影業(Amazon MGM Studios)也會在那個日期之前進行短暫的院線放映，但儘管主角的精心策劃的世界巡演令人心曠神怡，這部電影卻從未完全感覺到電影的氛圍：它的拍攝風格如同你對於從攝影師轉型為導演的莫里森(Rachel Morrison)（因拍攝《泥土之家》(Mudbound) 而獲得奧斯卡提名）和她選擇的攝影指導托德·本哈茲(Todd Benhazl)（《掠奪者》(Hustlers)）所期待的那樣吸引人，但他們那光輝、精確照明的影像卻並未集體積累出太多意義或力量；這部電影以高效的線性方式穿越其八年的時間線，但卻沒有特別的節奏。

不過，裡面是有生命的，這在很大程度上要歸功於羅利(Margaret Qualley)，她是一位可靠的好奇心和開放心態的演員，即使是相對模糊的角色——像是編劇茱莉亞·考克斯(Julia Cox)在此交給她的角色——也能賦予某種靈魂感。當我們遇見26歲的瑪雅(Maya)（羅利飾）時，她正在從瞬間心動的學者查理(Charlie)（加布里埃爾·巴索(Gabriel Basso)，仍在從《鄉村能源》(Hillbilly Energy) 中飾演J.D.·范斯的角色中恢復）那裡完成一筆Craigslist的床頭櫃購買，她幾乎算不上什麼：一名在波士頓工作的護士，沒有她願意提及的家庭，生活中也沒有除了繁重的醫院班次以外的其他事情。羅利(Margaret Qualley)在瑪雅的僵硬保留中找到了防衛的目的，並在查理的笨拙追求實際奏效時閃現出一絲快樂的光芒。

不久之後，他們便同居，並在維多利亞風格的公寓裡打造了一個完美的波希米亞風格愛巢。不久之後，他們向摯愛的親友們驚喜宣布婚禮，這讓查理的疲憊母親露絲（凱瑟琳·基納(Catherine Keener)）感到無言卻明顯的不安，並開始討論組建家庭的可能性——這是瑪雅一直發誓不會做的事情。隨後，一場全球大流行襲來，對我們的女主角來說，最糟糕的事情發生了。她陷入了無光的隧道般的痛苦悲傷中，拒絕了露絲和長期好友傑森（派翠克·史瓦辛格(Patrick Schwarzenegger)，在一個無足輕重的角色中）的陪伴，並在任何人能夠打擾她安排葬禮之前，迅速離開了小鎮。這是一種自私的創傷反應，奎莉（Margaret Qualley）似乎被痛苦壓得喘不過氣，卻幾乎理性地面對這一切。

然而，從這一點開始在《你生命中的愛》(Love of Your Life)中發生的一切，卻難以接受。我們跳躍了幾年，發現瑪雅——現在31歲，眼妝濃烈，經常抽煙——在里斯本的美麗街道上徘徊，雖然精緻的彩繪瓷磚和葡式蛋撻帶來些許情感上的慰藉，但顯然便宜的綠酒才是她的安慰。然而，當她與費利克斯（亞倫·皮爾(Aaron Pierre)）這位極其英俊的英國旅遊者邂逅時，她再次擁抱浪漫的可能性，首先跟隨他前往一處適合《康泰納仕》雜誌的葡萄牙鄉村度假屋，然後回到他在倫敦西部的優雅生活，還有可愛的小女兒。（他是一位關愛女兒的單身父親，與女孩的母親關係良好，免得你擔心這位夢中情人可能有任何性格缺陷。）

這一切都與現實生活毫不相似，這使得瑪雅的情感恢復越來越難以捉摸：我們在旁敲側擊中得知，她不知何故以遠程醫療的職業轉型資助這些延長的奢華旅行，而當她的在線治療師觀察到「我們真的在取得進展」時，我們只能相信她的話。與此同時，考克斯（Cox）的劇本越來越多地使用一刀切的治療語言，儘管奎莉作為表演者展現出自然的真誠，但隨著時間的推移，瑪雅似乎變得越來越不具體。

在故事的後期，《你生命中的愛》從一個讓瑪雅與露絲重聚的場景中獲得了令人歡欣的情感和真實感，凱瑟琳·基納（Catherine Keener）精彩地詮釋了這位在阿爾加維陽光下未能好好面對悲傷的女性所展現的破碎和明顯的疲憊。當她坦誠地剖析自己的傷痛，卻不再憤怒，背景是她家木材外牆的無光灰色，《你生命中的愛》終於重新與現實連結，且不會太遲。
